submission.justification: Unirradiated simulations (100k events each) show Sensor-T2 has clearly the best single-hit resolution: ~6.0 um at 150 um, compared with 9.1 um for T1 and 14.3 um for T3. This matches the 2025 summary (6.0/9.0/14.0 um). The T2 thickness scan gave 6.59 um at 50, 6.25 at 100, 6.09 at 125, ~5.8-6.1 at 150-175, 6.80 at 200 and 7.68 at 300 um. Running 160 um twice gave 5.76 and 6.04 um, so the statistical scatter is about ±0.2 um. The curve is therefore flat at about 6.0 um between roughly 125 and 175 um, and the 5.76 um point is not a real minimum. I chose 150 um, the centre of that optimum. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: none of the project documents contains radiation-hardness information for any candidate, and the simulation tool only models unirradiated sensors. The radiation-environment constraint is therefore UNVERIFIED. T2's resolution depends on large charge sharing, which radiation damage (charge trapping) typically degrades. From general field knowledge (not project documents), 3D-electrode sensors such as T3 are usually the radiation-hard choice for innermost layers. Before this recommendation is final, T2 needs a radiation qualification at the innermost-layer fluence and an irradiated simulation. If T2 fails that qualification, T3 should be re-evaluated as the fallback, even though its resolution is worse.

requirements.requirement: Goal: best possible single-hit spatial resolution
requirements.evidence: Among the three candidates in the unirradiated simulation, T2 at 150 um is best: ~6.0 um vs 9.1 um (T1) and 14.3 um (T3). The T2 thickness optimum is flat at 125-175 um, with ±0.2 um statistical scatter. Performance after irradiation was not simulated.
